subject: chemistry
title: Concentration in g/dm³
key_idea: Concentration is the mass of solute in a given volume of solution, measured in g/dm³. A concentrated solution has a high ratio of solute to volume. A dilute solution has a low ratio.

blocks.text: Many reactions take place in solution. The concentration tells you how much solute is dissolved in each unit of volume.

items.meaning: The solute dissolved in a liquid, such as water.
The mass of solute in a given volume of solution, for example in grams per dm³ (g/dm³).
A solution with a high ratio of solute to volume of solution.
A solution with a low ratio of solute to volume of solution.

items: More solute in the same volume gives a more concentrated solution.
Adding water makes a solution more dilute. The mass of solute stays the same, but the volume is larger.
To make an acid solution more concentrated (lower pH), add more acid or use less water.

blocks.text: Dilute and concentrated are not strong and weak

items: Dilute and concentrated describe the amount of acid in a given volume.
Strong and weak describe how much of the acid is ionised in solution.
A strong acid can be made into a concentrated solution or a dilute solution.
Concentration = how much solute is in a given volume of solution.
Concentrated means a high ratio of solute to volume. Dilute means a low ratio.
Dilute and concentrated are not the same as weak and strong.

blocks.text: The volume must be in dm³. Volumes in the question are usually in cm³, so convert first.

blocks.label: Concentration
blocks.formula: concentration = mass of solute ÷ volume of solution
where: concentration is in grams per dm³ (g/dm³)
mass of solute is in grams (g)
volume of solution is in dm³

items: To change cm³ to dm³, divide by 1000.
To change mg to g, divide by 1000.

blocks.text: 45 g of glucose is dissolved in water to make 150 cm³ of solution. Calculate the concentration in g/dm³.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating a concentration in g/dm³ from a mass and a volume in cm³.
diagram.question: **{m}** g of solute is dissolved in water to make **{v}** cm³ of solution. Calculate the concentration in g/dm³.

items: Always convert cm³ to dm³ by dividing by 1000.

sections.heading: Mass of solute and volume of solution

blocks.text: Rearrange the equation to find the mass of solute in a volume of solution, or the volume that holds a given mass.

blocks.label: Volume of solution
where: volume is in dm³ (multiply by 1000 for cm³)

blocks.text: Example: the mass of solute in 25 cm³ of a 21 g/dm³ solution is 21 × (25 ÷ 1000) = 0.525 g.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the mass of solute in a volume of solution of known concentration.
diagram.question: A solution has a concentration of **{c}** g/dm³. Calculate the mass of solute in **{v}** cm³ of this solution.

items: Volume = mass ÷ concentration. Multiply by 1000 to give cm³.
Check the units before and after: dm³ in the equation, cm³ only if asked.

checks.q: 12 g of salt is dissolved in water to make 400 cm³ of solution. Calculate the concentration in g/dm³.
Calculate the mass of solute in 250 cm³ of a solution with a concentration of 40 g/dm³.
What is the difference between a dilute and a concentrated solution of an acid?
checks.a: A dilute solution has a low ratio of acid to the volume of solution. A concentrated solution has a high ratio of acid to the volume of solution.

exam_phrases: (conversion of cm3 to dm3) (250 cm3 =) 250/1000 or 0.25 (dm3)
(conversion of mg to g) (125 mg =) 125/1000 or 0.125 (g)

mistakes.right: The volume must be in dm³. 800 cm³ = 0.8 dm³, so the mass is 0.8 × 258 = 206.4 g. A calculation with no volume conversion loses the conversion mark.

mistakes.wrong: River water has 125 mg per dm³, so 250 cm³ has 0.25 × 125 = 31 g.
mistakes.right: Convert mg to g as well as cm³ to dm³. 125 mg = 0.125 g, so the mass is 0.25 × 0.125 = 0.031 g.

mistakes.wrong: Mass = 206.4 g, so the answer is 206.4 g to 3 significant figures.
mistakes.right: Round to the number of significant figures asked for. To 3 significant figures, 206.4 g is 206 g.

worked_example.question:
A solution of potash alum has a concentration of 258 g/dm³.

Calculate the mass of potash alum needed to make 800 cm³ of a solution of potash alum with a concentration of 258 g/dm³.

Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: Marks are for the volume conversion, the multiplication, the unrounded value and the rounding.

mistakes.right: 28.4 ÷ 250 gives g per cm³. Convert the volume to dm³ first: 28.4 ÷ 0.250 = 113.6, which is 114 g/dm³. Leaving the volume in cm³ scores 2 of the 3 marks.

mistakes.wrong: Rounding 113.6 to 0.11 or 113 for 3 significant figures.
mistakes.right: 113.6 to 3 significant figures is 114. Rounding it incorrectly loses the first mark.

mistakes.wrong: The volume of 12 g/dm³ solution holding 9.0 g is 12 × 1000 ÷ 9 = 1333 cm³.
mistakes.right: Use volume = mass ÷ concentration = 9.0 ÷ 12 = 0.75 dm³. Then multiply by 1000 to give 750 cm³.

worked_example.question:
The sodium sulfate solution was made by dissolving 28.4 g of sodium sulfate in water to make 250 cm³ of solution.

Calculate the concentration of this solution in g dm⁻³.

Give your answer to three significant figures.
worked_example.tip: A correct final answer of 114 scores all three marks. The answer 0.114 scores 2.

exam_phrases: a dilute solution has a low ratio of acid to volume of solution
a strong acid can be made into a concentrated solution or a dilute solution
using a higher ratio of acid to water / using less water

mistakes.wrong: A strong acid must be concentrated.
mistakes.right: Strong and weak describe ionisation. A strong acid can be made into a concentrated solution or a dilute solution.

mistakes.wrong: To lower the pH of an acid solution, evaporate some of the water.
mistakes.right: Evaporating water from the current solution is ignored. Add more acid, or make a new solution with a higher ratio of acid to water.
Convert 25 cm³ to 0.025 dm³ first. Mass = 21 × 0.025 = 0.525 g, which is 0.53 g to 2 significant figures.

worked_example.question:
Barium chloride solutions with concentrations of 21 g / dm³ are suitable for experiments in school.

Calculate the mass of barium chloride that should be dissolved in 25 cm³ of water to make a solution with a concentration of 21 g / dm³.

Use the equation:

concentration = mass / volume

Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: An answer of 0.53 g scores all 3 marks. 0.525 g without the rounding scores 2.
